q: A camera is an optical instrument that forms and records an ____ of an object.
e: A camera forms and records an image of an object on film or on an electronic sensor. A convex lens throws a real inverted image onto that screen. Magnetic or thermal sensors are not the usual picture-taker.

q: The image may be recorded on film (or) it may be detected by an electronic ____ that stores the image digitally.
e: image and recorded have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of image would describe a different law.

q: A convex lens focuses the light from the object to form a real ____ image on the film or electronic sensor.
e: The camera's convex lens converges light to a real inverted image on the film or sensor. A concave lens diverges and will not form that real film image. Focusing then slides the lens distance until the image is sharp.

q: A diaphragm is placed behind the convex lens to control the amount of ____ energy falling on the film.
e: The diaphragm sits behind the convex lens and controls how much light energy hits the film. It changes aperture diameter, quoted as an f-number. The shutter, not the diaphragm, times the exposure.

q: The ____ is a circular opening through which the light passes.
e: Aperture is the circular opening light passes through. f-number is focal length over diameter; smaller f-number means a wider hole. Bright light wants a large f-number; dim light wants a small one.

q: The size or the diameter of the aperture is expressed in terms of ____.
e: f-number is focal length of the lens divided by aperture diameter. Small f-number, wide aperture, more light. Bright scenes need a large f-number so the hole is stopped down.

q: A ____ controls the time during which light enters the camera through the lens.
e: The shutter times how long light may enter through the lens. Shutter speed is quoted as that exposure time. A short exposure is a high shutter speed; focal length is a different control.

q: A camera consists of a focusing ring by which the distance between the lens and the film can be adjusted to obtain a ____ image on the film.
e: The focusing ring changes lens-to-film distance until the image is sharp. It is not a brightness control. Wrong distance leaves the picture blurred.

q: The film consists of a thin layer of chemical compounds of ____.
e: Photographic film is a thin layer of silver compounds. Those grains blacken where light hits. Digital work then swaps the whole layer for a pixel sensor.

q: In a digital camera, the film is replaced by an electronic sensor made up of millions of tiny ____ which response to light.
e: A digital sensor is millions of tiny pixels that respond to light. They store the image digitally, not analogously. Diodes or grains are not the name of those picture elements.
